name: Hostinger
oneLiner: Cheap fixed-size KVM servers on prepaid monthly, yearly or two-year terms, with root, Docker and one-click OpenClaw, Hermes and n8n templates.
whatItIs: Hostinger sells KVM virtual private servers in four fixed sizes: KVM 1 (1 vCPU / 4 GB / 50 GB), KVM 2 (2 / 8 / 100), KVM 4 (4 / 16 / 200) and KVM 8 (8 / 32 / 400). Every plan includes root access, a dedicated IPv4, NVMe disk, 4–32 TB of monthly bandwidth, weekly backups and a browser terminal. The server runs in one of 10 data centers, four in Europe, three of them in the EU.

It is a general-purpose VPS, not a sandbox API. You buy a machine by the month, or prepay 12 or 24 months for a lower monthly rate; there is no per-second meter, no pause that keeps memory, no fork, and no documented way to create one machine per task cheaply. You manage the operating system, updates and TLS yourself.

For agents, Hostinger's angle is one-click Docker templates rather than a managed runtime: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, n8n, Agent Zero, Dify and others can be deployed from the VPS dashboard. Hostinger also sells a separate managed AI automation plan that runs OpenClaw, Hermes, n8n or Paperclip (from $4.99/mo on a 24-month term, renewing at $11.99/mo; $10.99/mo on the 1-month term), which is not a VPS and is not priced by this card. A public API, CLI, Python/TypeScript SDKs and an official MCP server can manage the VPS itself.
whoFor: Readers who want one cheap, predictable, always-on Linux box for an agent or automation, are comfortable with a terminal, and do not need per-task sandboxes, pause/resume, forks or a managed agent backend.
isolation: A KVM virtual machine with its own kernel, root, Docker and a dedicated IPv4. Hostinger says VPS customers share a physical server, and CPU is burstable under a credit system rather than a permanently dedicated core.
sizes: Four fixed plans, no custom sizes: KVM 1 1 vCPU / 4 GB / 50 GB, KVM 2 2 / 8 / 100, KVM 4 4 / 16 / 200, KVM 8 8 / 32 / 400. CPU, RAM and disk cannot be upgraded separately; you move to a larger plan. KVM 8 is the top tier and cannot be upgraded, so growth means another VPS. No GPU on the VPS product; GPUs are a separate hourly product.

billing.model: Prepaid plan for a 1-, 12- or 24-month term. The monthly figure is the term total divided by its months, and the whole term is paid upfront.
billing.meter: A flat price per plan per month. There is no per-second or per-hour meter and no usage-based overage on the machine.
billing.stopped: A powered-off VPS keeps billing in full. Stopping is a compute-only power change; only disabling auto-renewal ends the charge at the end of the term.
billing.planFee: The plan price is the whole charge; there is no separate platform fee. A free domain for one year is included.
billing.minimum: One month of KVM 1 at the monthly-billed renewal, $19.49. The first month is discounted to $9.99. No free tier, and a card is required.

A.headline: $24.49 a month (one KVM 2 plan)
A.shape: KVM 2 (2 vCPU / 8 GB / 100 GB), one plan for the whole month

lines.label: The 1,000 tasks
lines.arithmetic: 1,000 × 10 min = 166.67 h, inside the 730 h month

notes: KVM 2 is the smallest plan with 2 vCPU and 4 GiB; it also brings 8 GB and 100 GB, so the size is a superset rather than an exact fit.
One machine runs the tasks one after another. 166.67 hours is well inside a month, so the plan covers the work.
Buying a fresh VPS per task would mean 1,000 monthly plans, which is why this workload is not a Hostinger use case.
If this is a single month and the plan is not renewed, the first-period price is $13.99; the card uses the $24.49 renewal because A is a monthly workload.
A.flag: This assumes one plan running the tasks one after another. Running them in parallel, or a fresh server per task, would need one monthly plan per machine.

B.headline: $42.99 a month
notes: The 4 vCPU and 8 GiB ask fits KVM 4, whose 16 GB and 200 GB are larger than needed.
On the 24-month term the renewal is $28.99/mo, but $695.76 is paid upfront for two years.
Average CPU is 10%, below the 60% credit baseline, so the CPU credit system does not throttle this workload.

C.headline: $24.49 a month, even while stopped
C.shape: KVM 2 (2 vCPU / 8 GB / 100 GB), 90 running + 640 stopped hours

lines.label: Stopped hours
lines.arithmetic: 640 h at no extra charge, and no credit either

notes: Stopping the VPS keeps the disk and the files, but it does not stop billing. The month costs the same as B's smaller plan, whether the machine is on for 90 hours or 730.
There is no pause with memory: a stop powers the machine off, so a running process is lost.
On the 24-month term the renewal is $14.99/mo, paid upfront as $359.76.
C.flag: Workload C's 640 idle hours look cheap on a per-hour sandbox and are not cheap here: the full plan bills through them.

facts.label: Legal entity
facts.value: Hostinger International Limited, a Cyprus private limited company, for most countries including the EU. UK customers contract with Hostinger UK Limited; some countries use Hostinger Global S.à r.l in Luxembourg or Hostinger Pte Ltd in Singapore.

facts.label: Funding
facts.value: No outside funding round or valuation is published. The company describes its 2004 origin as bootstrapped; that is history, not a statement about current ownership.

source.quote: A group of young entrepreneurs bootstrapped a personal company and named it Hosting Media.

facts.label: Uptime promise
facts.value: A 99.9% monthly service uptime guarantee, with a 5% credit of the monthly hosting fee if Hostinger misses it. Scheduled maintenance and customer-caused interruptions are excluded.

source.quote: We offer a Service uptime guarantee of 99.9% (“Service Uptime Guarantee”) of available time per month.

facts.label: Compliance
facts.value: GDPR and PCI DSS v4.0.1 are also listed. No SOC 2 report is listed.

facts.label: Status page
facts.value: A public status page lists incidents and scheduled maintenance, including VPS node maintenance.

source.quote: Scheduled maintenance is currently in progress. We will provide updates as necessary.

well: One always-on agent on a normal Linux box: KVM 2 gives 2 vCPU, 8 GB, 100 GB, root, Docker and a public IPv4 for $24.49 a month.
A non-coder who wants OpenClaw, Hermes or n8n running quickly: the VPS dashboard has one-click Docker templates and a web terminal for the rest.
A predictable bill: the plan price is fixed, 4–32 TB of outbound data is included, and there is no per-GiB overage charge.
European hosting with France, Germany, Lithuania and the UK, three of them in the EU, plus a 99.9% SLA, ISO 27001 and a DPA.
badly: Many short-lived tasks or one machine per user: there is no per-second billing and no cheap programmatic create/destroy loop.
Pause, resume or fork: stopping loses memory and still bills, and the single snapshot expires after a day.
A team that needs SSO, a hard account spend cap, a full audit log or scoped API keys.
Nested virtualisation, a custom OS image, a GPU inside the VPS, or a separate volume that outlives the machine.

usability.dashboard: Yes: a VPS dashboard with status and resource graphs, a browser console and Hostinger Agent, Docker Manager, snapshots and backups, firewall, SSH keys, OS reinstall, DNS manager, API tokens and plan upgrade.
usability.withoutCode: Partly. The purchase and an application template such as OpenClaw, Hermes or n8n are click-through, but connecting a model key, a chat channel or a domain usually needs the terminal. Hostinger's separate managed AI automation plan is the no-terminal product.
usability.signup: A Hostinger account and a card. There is no free tier or starting credit; the exit is a 30-day money-back guarantee, with a 180-day cooldown after a VPS refund.
usability.docs: A large support knowledge base plus a separate API reference with OpenAPI-generated CLI, SDK and MCP docs. The VPS dashboard also embeds Hostinger Agent, an AI console that runs commands in natural language.
tripsUp: The advertised $6.49–$25.99 prices are 24-month introductory prices paid upfront; the 1-month renewal is $19.49–$73.99.
The first month is discounted even on the 1-month term, so the second invoice is the real ongoing price.
A stopped VPS still bills in full.
CPU is burstable under a credit system; a long build can be throttled after about three hours at full load.
There is one snapshot and it expires after one day.
The server location cannot be changed in place; you backup and reinstall in another data center.
No custom OS image and no nested virtualisation.
Docker Manager is experimental and only works with Docker OS templates.

caveats.issue: The advertised price is not the ongoing price
caveats.detail: The VPS page was in a Black Friday sale on 2026-10-30 and leads with 24-month introductory prices ($6.49–$25.99/mo), with the full term paid upfront. The 1-month term renews at $19.49–$73.99/mo. The card uses the 1-month renewal; the 12- and 24-month renewals are lower but prepaid.

caveats.issue: "Dedicated resources" sits beside a shared host and a CPU credit throttle
caveats.detail: The VPS page says "Get dedicated resources" and the Docker page says "Guaranteed resources", while the hosting agreement says VPS customers "share a server with other customers" and the CPU credit article says capacity is cut when credits run out. The CPU is not a permanently dedicated core.

evidence.quote: Get dedicated resources, root access, and the freedom to configure your server your way.
If you purchase VPS, you will share a server with other customers, but you will have full control over your server space and the complete configuration of your virtual instance on the server.
40% on KVM 1 and 30% on KVM 2, KVM 4 and KVM 8

caveats.issue: Hostinger's own pages disagree on the throttled CPU floor
caveats.detail: The CPU credit article says 40% on KVM 1 and 30% on the larger plans. A separate CPU-limit FAQ says 5% to 20% depending on the plan. The model uses the credit article's figures and treats the FAQ as unresolved.

evidence.quote: 40% on KVM 1 and 30% on KVM 2, KVM 4 and KVM 8
It is limited only when the credit balance is empty, to between 5% and 20% of capacity depending on your plan.

caveats.issue: "Change location anytime" is not true for a running VPS
caveats.detail: The VPS marketing page says you can move a VPS to any of the 10 locations. The support article says the location is fixed after setup and the only alternative is to back up and reinstall in another data center.

evidence.quote: For VPS, the server location is fixed after initial setup. As an alternative, you can backup and reinstall the VPS on a different data center.

caveats.issue: The only snapshot expires after one day
caveats.detail: A manual snapshot captures the whole VPS, but only one can exist, a new one overwrites it, and it is deleted after 1 day. Weekly backups are the longer-lived protection, and restoring either overwrites the current server.

caveats.issue: Stopping does not stop the bill
caveats.detail: The stop endpoint calls it a compute-only power change that does not affect billing. A machine that is off for 640 hours still pays the full monthly plan, and its memory and running processes are gone.

caveats.issue: The managed agent plan is a different product
caveats.detail: Hostinger's managed AI automation plan runs OpenClaw, Hermes, n8n or Paperclip (from $4.99/mo on 24 months, $10.99/mo monthly); it is not a VPS plan. The VPS templates give root and a persistent disk but no managed automatic updates, AI credits or Telegram pairing; those are terminal work.

caveats.issue: Hostinger quotes GB, the calculator uses GiB
caveats.detail: Hostinger labels RAM and disk in GB; the calculator's fields are GiB. The card maps 8/16/32 GB and 50–400 GB 1:1 to GiB. If those are decimal GB, 32 GB is 29.8 GiB and the largest plan is just under the 32 GiB mark. A/B/C asks are smaller and unaffected.

strengths: A full Linux VM with root, Docker, a dedicated IPv4 and 100 GB of disk for $24.49 a month on the monthly-billed term.
One-click Docker templates for OpenClaw, Hermes Agent and n8n, with a web terminal and Hostinger Agent for the rest.
Four European locations, three in the EU, a 99.9% SLA with a 5% credit, ISO 27001 and a DPA.
4–32 TB of monthly outbound data with no per-GiB overage bill; the penalty is a 10 Mbps throttle.
An unusually complete automation surface for a budget VPS: dashboard, CLI, Python/TypeScript SDKs, REST API and an official MCP server.
Free weekly backups with two weekly and two daily restore points.
